subject: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Sep 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps

Hi Jordan & Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciated the walkthrough of your search+QA pipeline and the objectives you laid out. Quick recap from our side and the proposed next steps so we all have the same priorities.

Top pain points you shared:
- Latency spikes for embeddings/reranking at peak traffic (esp. during end-of-day analytics).
- High per-token cost on the current hosted setup when you batch multiple queries and hit long context windows.
- Difficulty getting structured outputs consistently (JSON fields) from the current LLM integration — causes downstream parsing failures.

Goals for Q4:
1) Reduce median reranking latency by 40% at 95th percentile.
2) Cut per-query cost by ~25% through batching + KV caching/quantization.
3) Get reliable structured outputs for order-extraction and product-entity tagging (schema validation).

Product fit & integration notes we discussed:
- SDK changes: we recommend the new Redwood JS SDK v2 call pattern (streaming + function-calling wrappers). This will let you: stream tokens to the client, call your existing entity-extraction function via function-calling, and accept structured JSON outputs with schema enforcement.
- Function calling: we can add a light wrapper so your existing entity-extract service (internal microservice) can be invoked directly during generation to improve fidelity.
- Streaming: use streaming for UI response-first experiences; combine with prefix KV cache for repeated context to lower latency.
- Structured outputs: Redwood's structured-output mode + schema validation reduces post-processing errors. We can preview using your product-entity schema.
- Embeddings & reranking: suggest switching to our optimized 1536-d embeddings with batch-acceleration; combine with incremental reranking (top-k) to reduce model calls.

Attachments: I attached a short integration proposal and a sample pipeline config.

Next steps (proposed):
- Rishi to scope a short POC (2 weeks) for reranking + structured outputs using a subset of your traffic (we'll propose exact endpoints).
- Acme to share a small sample dataset and the product-entity schema (Priya).
- Schedule a technical sync: 30–45m next Tue or Wed with your platform/infra + our SEs (Rishi & Vivek).

Would love confirmation of the dataset share and two preferred time slots for the tech sync.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

Attachments:
- redwood-integration-proposal.pdf (3 pages)
- acme-malpipeline-sample.json (sample records)

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Sep 2027 17:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is great, and aligns with what we discussed. A few quick clarifications from our end: 

- Dataset: we can share a ~10k-record sample export (anonymized) by EOD tomorrow. Priya is looping in the data steward to confirm.
- Tech sync times: Tue 09/14 10:00–10:45 PT or Wed 09/15 14:00–14:45 PT both work; prefer Tue if possible.
- For the POC, we want to confirm success metrics up front: 95th percentile latency under X ms (we'll put numbers in the doc) and structured-output schema pass rate >= 98%.

Also tagging one internal ask: can Redwood's POC run against a private sandbox (VPC) or do you need us to proxy traffic through our staging? Security is a requirement.

I'll confirm dataset timing once Priya checks with the steward.

—Jordan
Director, Search Platform
Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps

Perfect — Tue 09/14 10:00 PT locked. Rishi & Vivek will join for the tech sync.

Quick answers: 
- POC environment: we can run the POC in a customer-managed VPC (Redwood Private) or via a staged integration in our hosted sandbox depending on your compliance needs. For Acme, given security notes, our VPC option is recommended — we'll include a KMS/HSM integration option in the POC proposal.
- Success metrics: agreed — we'll propose concrete latency targets in the POC SOW. The 98% schema pass target is reasonable; we'll instrument evals and provide per-prompt failure logs.

Action items assigned:
- Acme: share anonymized sample data + product-entity schema (Priya) — target: 2027-09-10 EOD.
- Redwood (Rishi): draft POC scope & SOW + environment options — target: 2027-09-12.
- Redwood (Vivek): prepare a short demo of function-calling + structured-output using a small toy dataset for Tue's call.

If anything changes on timing, flag it here. Looking forward to the sync.

Best,
Marissa
